metadata.name: forced-source
metadata.description: Phase H — Odum's forcing functions (Systems Ecology Fig. 7-2) as ONE waveform vocabulary attached in TWO places. A sinusoidal solar source drives a producer; a square-wave harvest drains it; a step change in the drain's rate arrives partway through the run.

_why_one_vocabulary: Odum draws eleven forcing annotations, but they are not eleven mechanisms. They are a node-value versus edge-rate distinction crossed with a carrier distinction, and GSSK already models carriers as Position 1 on nodes and edges. So the eleven collapse to one vocabulary times two attachment points: forcing on a NODE drives its held value (Odum X/N, a force), forcing on an EDGE drives its rate k (Odum J, a flow). See docs/adr/0006.
_why_stage_times_matter: Every waveform here is evaluated at the RK4 stage times, not once per step. Sampling once per step would leave the forcing first-order while the state is fourth-order — the run would still complete and the trajectory would still look smooth. tests/test_forcing.c catches it with a convergence study: this model's shape gives ~16x error reduction per halving of dt, and ~2x if the forcing is sampled per step.

nodes._note: The annual solar cycle. phase is a TIME offset in days and is SUBTRACTED, so 91.25 (a quarter period) delays the peak to midsummer at t=182.5 rather than t=91.25. min:0 clamps the winter trough at zero, because insolation does not go negative — the clamp is applied after the formula, not folded into it.
A storage node CANNOT carry a forcing block: its value is the integral of its flows, so forcing it is a contradiction. GSSK_Init rejects it rather than ignoring it.

edges._note: Unforced. flow = k x sun(t), so the seasonal signal reaches the producer through the SOURCE's value — Odum's X/N attachment.

Odum's J attachment: forcing on an EDGE drives its rate k. A six-day cropping window every thirty days — k alternates between mean+amplitude (0.04) and mean-amplitude (0.0), so the drain is fully off between harvests. params.k is what an unforced edge would use and is ignored while forcing is present.
A step change in maintenance cost at day 180 — a regime shift, Odum's step forcing. Before t_on the rate is v0; at and after t_on it is v1. The boundary is closed on the right.
